entry.title: NS-Leibniz bialgebras, the Yang--Baxter equation and relative Rota--Baxter operators
entry.summary: We introduce NS-Leibniz bialgebras and establish their equivalence with matched pairs and Manin triples of NS-Leibniz algebras. In the coboundary case, skew-symmetric solutions of the NS-Leibniz Yang--Baxter equation yield NS-Leibniz bialgebras and correspond to $\mathcal{O}$-operators for the dual regular representation. We study quasi-triangular and factorizable structures, and relate factorizable tensors to quadratic Rota--Baxter NS-Leibniz algebras of any fixed nonzero weight. We also construct compatible bialgebra structures from skew-adjoint Nijenhuis operators commuting with the Rota--Baxter operator.

entry.title: Locally unital $C^*$-algebras and limitations of seminorm criteria for compact operators
entry.summary: We study the problem of geometric characterization of Banach-compact and $\mathcal A$-compact operators on Hilbert $C^*$-modules in terms of uniform structures generated by seminorms. Previously, such a criterion for $\mathcal A$-compactness of adjointable operators was obtained by Troitsky for countably generated range modules with a suitable system of seminorms. Using locally unital $C^*$-algebras as modules over themselves, we establish fundamental limitations of such characterizations. Namely, we show that for nonunital locally unital $C^*$-algebras not only does Troitsky's criterion fail to extend, but, more generally, no system of seminorms can characterize $\mathcal A$-precompactness by total boundedness, nor Banach-compactness of bounded operators or $\mathcal A$-compactness of adjointable operators by total boundedness of the images of the unit ball. Moreover, the same statement holds for Hilbert $C^*$-modules $\mathcal N$ whenever the algebra $\mathbf K(\mathcal N)$ of $\mathcal A$-compact operators is locally unital and nonunital. We also study Troitsky-type systems of seminorms and their relation to $\mathcal A$-precompactness. We prove that every $\mathcal A$-precompact subset is totally bounded with respect to the strongest of such structures. Consequently, for Hilbert $C^*$-modules admitting a standard frame, all the corresponding notions of total boundedness coincide.

entry.title: On two counterexamples in the geometry of numbers
entry.summary: We give counterexamples to two optimization problems in dimensions eight and nine. 1. The Cartesian-product problem posed by Cassels for critical determinants and later formulated by Zong for lattice packings and for packings allowing translations but not rotations: whether the corresponding product inequalities are always equalities. The counterexample also disproves the natural product formula for unrestricted congruent packings. 2. A question raised by Sarnak and formulated as a conjecture in Chiu: whether, among unit-volume flat tori, height is minimized by a lattice maximizing the length of its shortest nonzero vector.

entry.title: Black-hole formation and thermalization in open JT gravity
entry.summary: Black-hole formation is expected, via holography, to correspond to thermalization in the boundary theory. For open quantum systems, an initial pure state generically evolves into a mixed state irreversibly, suggesting that horizon formation in the bulk should arise. In this paper, we extend the holographic Lindblad prescription to a non-Markovian setting and apply it to JT gravity coupled to a scalar field. Using numerical simulations in the semiclassical and high-temperature regime, we demonstrate the dynamical formation of black holes.

entry.title: Limit Theorems and Optimal Policies for Flock Flight through Poisson Forests
entry.summary: Inspired by birds flying through cluttered environments, Karaman and Frazzoli showed that high-speed flight through an ergodic random forest exhibits an ultimate speed limit: above a critical speed, almost surely no infinite collision-free trajectory exists for a single bird. This paper formulates a corresponding bulk-transport problem for many birds. We construct an explicit directed corridor network in a Poisson disk forest and impose a common temporal headway at its waypoints. The maximum current equals a minimum vertex-cut capacity and is achieved by repeated flight along vertex-disjoint paths. The same schedule maximizes completed traversals at every finite horizon, with constant forward speed and no internal waiting. For a forest belt of fixed depth, exact transverse superadditivity yields an almost-sure deterministic current-density limit. A uniform shape theorem for an asymmetric planar dual identifies the current when depth and width grow together. For diverging depth bounded by a constant times width, this current equals the width-first, depth-second limit and is independent of the positive aspect ratio. When diagonal corridors are available, bulk current is positive at sufficiently low obstacle intensity and zero at sufficiently high intensity. For stochastic demand, an upstream admission queue is stable at every rate below the finite-network capacity.

entry.title: Symmetric Policy Optimization for Zero-Sum Markov Games
entry.summary: We propose a simple and symmetric method for policy optimization in discounted zero-sum Markov games. The method, termed symmetric policy iteration, operates by evaluating the joint policy and solving the corresponding regularized matrix game at each iteration. By employing a diminishing sequence of regularization strengths, we establish the global linear convergence of the proposed method to the optimal value function and the saddle point. In particular, the method does not require solving any standalone Markov decision process throughout policy optimization, and is symmetric in the sense that it stays invariant regardless of whether we are solving the min-max or the max-min version of the game. To the best of our knowledge, this appears to be the first simple and symmetric policy-based method attaining global convergence for discounted zero-sum Markov games.

entry.title: Generalized Fermat equation over number fields
entry.summary: Let $K$ be a number field and $A,B,C\in\mathcal{O}_K\setminus\{0\}$. Put $S_K=\{\mathfrak{P}:\mathfrak{P}\mid2\}$ and $S_K'=\{\mathfrak{q}:\mathfrak{q}\mid2ABC\}$. We establish two criteria for the non-existence of non-trivial solutions of $Ax^p+By^p=Cz^p$ over $K$ for sufficiently large prime exponents $p$. Both criteria use a valuation bound on the $S_K'$-unit equation at a fixed $\mathfrak{P}\in S_K$. The first excludes all non-trivial solutions in $K^3$ when $v_{\mathfrak{P}}(A)=v_{\mathfrak{P}}(B)=m$ and $v_{\mathfrak{P}}(C)=m+k$, with $k>4v_{\mathfrak{P}}(2)$. The second, under an explicit nonvanishing condition on the coefficient valuations, excludes solutions $(a,b,c)\in(K^\times)^3$ whose $\mathfrak{P}$-valuations are not all equal. In particular, it excludes non-trivial primitive integral solutions with $\mathfrak{P}\mid abc$. Neither criterion restricts the residue degree of $\mathfrak{P}$. Both criteria hold unconditionally over every totally real field; over general number fields, we assume residual modularity and Eichler--Shimura-type conjectures. The first criterion covers a new coefficient range. In particular, under the corresponding $S_K$-unit bound, $x^p+y^p=2^rz^p$ has no non-trivial solutions in $K^3$ for each fixed $r\geq5$ and sufficiently large prime $p$. This bound holds for a set of real quadratic fields of relative density $1$. For a family of imaginary quadratic fields of relative density $5/6$, we explicitly determine the $S_K$-unit solutions and verify the valuation bound for both criteria when $A,B,C\in\{\pm2^r:r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}\}$, including the same $r\geq5$ conclusion.

entry.title: Thompson's groups and Teichmüller modular groups of generalized Cantor sets
entry.summary: Thompson's groups, which are denoted by $F, T$ and $V$, were introduced by R. Thompson. It is known that they are related to various fields in mathematics. In this paper, we discuss Thompson's groups $F, T$ and $V$ in Teichmüller modular groups of Teichmüller spaces of generalized Cantor sets with certain conditions by using a quasiconformal geometric method. Moreover, we show that groups corresponding to $F$ and $T$ act properly discontinuously on such Teichmüller spaces. We also show the same results for the asymptotic Teichmüller space. E. de Faria, F. P. Gardiner and W. J. Harvey show similar results on Thompson's group $F$ and asymptotic Teichmüller spaces. So, our results are improvement of them. We also discuss the actions of Thompson's groups on other spaces which we call \lq\lq pre-Tiechmüller spaces" of generalized Cantor sets. Especially, we show that the action of a group which is isomorphic to Thompson's group $V$ on the pre-Teichüller space is not properly discontinuous while groups isomorphic to $F$ and $T$ act properly discontinuously. Finally, we construct infinitely many distinct Teichmüller spaces of generalized Cantor sets where our results can apply.

entry.title: Enhancement of superconducting stiffness in hybrid superconducting-metallic bilayers
entry.summary: Boosting superconductivity by metallic reservoirs is the essence of Kivelson's bilayer proposal. One layer provides pairing to the electrons, while the weakly coupled metal provides additional phase coherence to those pairs by mediating extended-range pair-pair coupling. Demonstrating significant and unambiguous performance gains with strong-coupling methods for such set-ups had been difficult. In the present work, we study these systems doped away from half-filling, corresponding to a partially spin-polarized 1D Anderson- or Kondo-lattice. We show that this breaks the coexistence of dominant superconducting and density-density correlations decisively in favour or the former. Consequently, we provide evidence that in this doped regime, superconducting near-long-range order is not precluded by a small charge-gap in the thermodynamic limit, as we have recently shown to be the case at half-filling [J. E. Ebot \textit{et al.}, Phys. Rev. B \textbf{113}, 174530 (2026)]. We study the complex manner in which the enhancement of superconductivity in the pairing layer depends on the parameters of the metal, and especially that both pairing-limited and stiffness-limited regimes may appear in these systems. In addition to superconducting bilayers, our results are relevant, via a particle-hole transformation, for heavy-fermion Kondo-lattice materials in magnetic fields, as we provide previously lacking insight on the competition between antiferromagnetic and easy-plane magnetism, as well as a route for comprehensive indirect tests of Kivelson's bilayer proposal well beyond previous capabilities.

entry.title: Topological Interpretations in Anisotropic Kerr-Newman-AdS Black Hole Thermodynamics
entry.summary: The interplay between black hole thermodynamics and topology provides a strong, coordinate-independent framework for discovering the underlying structure of black hole phase transitions as well as their universal features. We explore the thermodynamic topology of the anisotropic Kerr-Newman-AdS black hole using Duan's $φ$-mapping theory and a complex residue approach. By creating the generalized off-shell free energy, we propose a thermodynamic vector field in the parameter space with zero points corresponding to equilibrium black hole states. The winding numbers associated with these defects are utilized to calculate the black hole's global topological number. We begin with an analysis of the entire anisotropic Kerr-Newman-AdS black hole, followed by two limiting examples. Setting the anisotropic parameter $K = 0$ produces the Kerr-Newman-AdS black hole, while eliminating the AdS contribution produces the Kerr-Newman black hole. The anisotropic Kerr-Newman-AdS and Kerr-Newman-AdS black holes have a single thermodynamic defect with winding number $+1$, which results in $W = +1$. In contrast, the Kerr-Newman black hole has two defects with winding numbers $+1$ and $-1$, which result in a vanishing global topological number, $W = 0$. These findings show that the AdS contribution alters the global topological classification, but the anisotropic matter studied here preserves the topological class of the Kerr-Newman-AdS black hole. As an analogous limiting instance, we further study a Kiselev-type black hole, analyzing the circumstances in which its metric reduces to a charged black-hole geometry and how the thermodynamic topology reflects this reduction. Finally, we use the complex residue approach on the anisotropic Kerr-Newman-AdS black hole.

entry.title: Particle transformers for identifying Lorentz-boosted Higgs bosons decaying to a pair of W bosons
entry.summary: A novel deep neural network classifier, a ``Particle transformer'' (PaRT), is introduced for the identification of highly Lorentz-boosted resonances reconstructed as single, multipronged jets in measurements and searches performed by the CMS Collaboration at the CERN LHC. Based on a self-attention mechanism that allows the model to weigh the importance of different particles, PaRT is trained on a wide variety of topologies, notably demonstrating strong performance for the first time on jets originating from boosted Higgs boson decays to W bosons. The PaRT algorithm achieves a tagging efficiency of more than 50% for such jets at a background efficiency of 1%, while maintaining decorrelation from the jet mass. A calibration is performed in proton-proton collision data collected by CMS at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV, with a data set corresponding to a total luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$. Data-to-simulation selection efficiency scale factors are measured to be in the 0.9$-$1.0 range, with relative uncertainties between 7 and 23%. The tagging capability of PaRT enhances the sensitivity of standard model measurements and searches for beyond-the-standard-model resonances decaying to hadronic diboson systems.

entry.title: Invert4TVG: A Temporal Video Grounding Framework with Inversion Tasks Preserving Action Understanding Ability
entry.summary: Temporal Video Grounding (TVG) aims to localize video segments corresponding to a given textual query, which often describes human actions. However, we observe that current methods, usually optimizing for high temporal Intersection-over-Union (IoU), frequently struggle to accurately recognize or understand the underlying actions in both the video and query, thus reducing the effectiveness of these methods. To address this, we propose a novel TVG framework that integrates inversion-based TVG as auxiliary objectives to maintain the model's action understanding ability. We introduce three kinds of inversion TVG tasks derived from the original TVG annotations: (1) Verb Completion, predicting masked verbs (actions) in queries given video segments; (2) Action Recognition, identifying query-described actions; and (3) Video Description, generating descriptions containing query-relevant actions given video segments. These inversion tasks are entirely derived from the original TVG tasks and are probabilistically integrated with them within a reinforcement learning framework. By leveraging carefully designed reward functions, the model preserves its ability to understand actions, thereby improving the accuracy of temporal grounding. Experiments show our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, achieving a 7.1\% improvement in R1@0.7 on Charades-STA for a 3B model.

entry.title: Rethinking Group Recommender Systems in the Era of Generative AI: From One-Shot Recommendations to Conversational Group Decision Support
entry.summary: More than twenty-five years ago, early ideas emerged on how to design systems that provide recommendations to groups of users rather than individuals. Since then, a wide range of algorithmic approaches has been proposed to elicit individual preferences, aggregate them, and generate group recommendations. However, despite this substantial body of work, relatively few examples of real-world group recommender systems are in use. This observation invites reflection on the assumptions of the academic research, particularly regarding how inter-group communication unfolds and how recommendation-supported decisions should be made. In this essay, we suggest that some of these assumptions and corresponding system designs may not fully align with users' needs or expectations. We therefore outline a forward-looking perspective that explores how insights from group-decision making research and recent advances in Generative AI, including systems such as ChatGPT, could better inform the design of group recommender systems. As one possible direction, we consider settings in which human group members interact and exchange information through a chat based interface, while an AI-based agent supports the decision-making process. Such an approach may contribute to design more natural group and system interactions, and could help facilitate a broader adoption of group recommender systems in practice.

entry.title: Centro-Affine Differential Geometry and the Log-Minkowski Problem
entry.summary: We interpret the log-Brunn-Minkowski conjecture of Böröczky-Lutwak-Yang-Zhang as a spectral problem in centro-affine differential geometry. In particular, we show that the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator coincides with the centro-affine Laplacian, thus obtaining a new avenue for tackling the conjecture using insights from affine differential geometry. As every strongly convex hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a centro-affine unit-sphere, it has constant centro-affine Ricci curvature equal to $n-2$, in stark contrast to the standard weighted Ricci curvature of the associated metric-measure space, which will in general be negative. In particular, we may use the classical argument of Lichnerowicz and a centro-affine Bochner formula to give a new proof of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality. For origin-symmetric convex bodies enjoying fairly generous curvature pinching bounds (improving with dimension), we are able to show global uniqueness in the $L^p$- and log-Minkowski problems, as well as the corresponding global $L^p$- and log-Minkowski conjectured inequalities. As a consequence, we resolve the isomorphic version of the log-Minkowski problem: for any origin-symmetric convex body $\bar K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, there exists an origin-symmetric convex body $K$ with $\bar K \subset K \subset 8 \bar K$, so that $K$ satisfies the log-Minkowski conjectured inequality, and so that $K$ is uniquely determined by its cone-volume measure $V_K$. If $\bar K$ is not extremely far from a Euclidean ball to begin with, an analogous isometric result, where $8$ is replaced by $1+ε$, is obtained as well.

entry.title: Fast rates for the classification of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck paths
entry.summary: In binary classification problems, plug-in classifiers can sometimes achieve faster excess risk rates than the underlying estimation rate. In this work, we study a supervised classification problem based on repeated independent observations of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck paths, with both time-homogeneous and time-inhomogeneous drifts. We show that, under a suitable separation condition on the class-dependent drifts, a plug-in classifier attains an excess risk of quadratic order in the corresponding parametric or nonparametric estimation error. The theoretical approach utilizes the Wiener chaos representation and spectral theory to characterize the log-likelihood ratio as a quadratic form of Gaussian random variables, enabling a precise analysis of margin behaviour and deviation results. This extends the fast-rate results from classification problems with linear discriminant models and Gaussian white noise models to dynamical diffusion systems with Gaussian structure.

entry.title: Approximation of the relaxed Euler system at the level of the compressible Navier-Stokes equations
entry.summary: We study the global well-posedness of the Cauchy problem in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\geq2$, for the relaxed compressible Euler system with a Maxwell-type constitutive law for the stress tensor. We show that the corresponding compressible Navier-Stokes solutions serve as both relaxation limits and large-time asymptotic profiles of the global relaxed Euler solutions constructed here. Given a Navier-Stokes background satisfying suitable boundedness and decay assumptions, we construct global smooth relaxed Euler solutions for each fixed $α\in(0,1]$ and sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$. Here, the background need not be small. After subtracting the stress initial layer, the approximation error is $O(\varepsilon^α)$ uniformly in time. Under suitable additional conditions on the initial perturbations, this error decays in $L^2$ faster than the decay of standard Navier-Stokes background, uniformly in $\varepsilon$, identifying the background solution as a large-time asymptotic profile. As an application, we obtain the corresponding small-data results using classical Navier-Stokes theory to verify the background assumptions.

entry.title: Standardly stratified structures from tilting modules
entry.summary: Characteristic tilting modules play a central role in the theory of standardly stratified algebras, for instance in Ringel duality. They are constructed from the standard modules, which are determined by a partial order on the simple modules. In this paper, we characterize characteristic tilting modules intrinsically. We show that a tilting module is a characteristic tilting module if and only if the matrix of composition multiplicities of its indecomposable direct summands is triangular with respect to suitable orderings of the summands and of the simple modules. In this case, the standard modules and all the corresponding partial orders are recovered from the tilting module. As an application, we prove that the tilting correspondence of Geiss, Leclerc and Schröer between a GLS path algebra and its associated hereditary algebra restricts to a bijection between characteristic tilting modules. In particular, we obtain GLS path algebras that are not quasi-hereditary with respect to any partial order but for which every tilting module is a characteristic tilting module.

entry.title: Dually flat structure of von Mises-Fisher distributions
entry.summary: The von Mises--Fisher (vMF) distribution is the natural exponential family analogue of the normal distribution on the unit hypersphere. We bring together previous results of its dually flat structure and establish new results on the information geometry of the family of vMF distributions. In particular, we characterize the exponential and mixture autoparallel submanifolds, and give the classification of doubly autoparallel submanifolds. Furthermore, we derive explicit formulas for the unique minimizers of the Kullback-Leibler divergence on these submanifolds and establish the corresponding projection theorems.

entry.title: Rotation Equivariant Mamba for Vision Tasks
entry.summary: Rotation equivariance is an important structural prior for a broad range of vision tasks, particularly in domains such as remote sensing and medical imaging where objects have no canonical orientation, yet it remains notably absent from current Mamba-based vision architectures. Despite the success of Mamba in natural language processing and its growing adoption in computer vision, existing visual Mamba models fail to account for rotational symmetry in their design. This omission renders them sensitive to image rotations, thereby constraining their robustness and cross-task generalization. To address this limitation, we incorporate rotation symmetry, an important geometric prior in many visual domains, into Mamba-based architectures. Specifically, we introduce EQ-VMamba, the first rotation equivariant visual Mamba architecture for vision tasks. The core components of EQ-VMamba include a carefully designed rotation equivariant cross-scan strategy and group Mamba blocks. Moreover, we provide a rigorous theoretical analysis of the intrinsic equivariance error, demonstrating that the proposed architecture enforces end-to-end rotation equivariance under the p4 rotation group. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks---including high-level image classification, mid-level semantic segmentation, and low-level image super-resolution---demonstrate that EQ-VMamba consistently improves rotation robustness and achieves superior or competitive performance compared to non-equivariant baselines on most benchmarks, while requiring 40-70% fewer parameters. These results indicate that embedding rotation equivariance not only effectively bolsters the robustness of visual Mamba models against rotation transformations, but also improves accuracy on data exhibiting rotational symmetry, with substantially improved parameter efficiency. Code is available at https://github.com/zhongchenzhao/EQ-VMamba.

entry.title: Optimal Value Inference for Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: We study offline inference for the optimal value in reinforcement learning under finite state and action spaces. Two new nuisances are derived as fixed points of a self-induced Bellman equation, in which we approximate the maximum Bellman operator by its softmax correspondence. We propose a debiased estimator through the Neyman orthogonality and establish its asymptotic normality under diverging horizons even when the behavior policy changes with time, as long as the nuisances have the statistical rates that can be achieved by many machine learning methods. We provide a concrete estimating procedure for these nuisances and show they can lead to valid inference. Synthetic experiments validate the numerical performance of our inference method, and we implement it in real-life decision-making problems, including bike repositioning and AI agentic tool use.

entry.title: ACAM-J-MARS: Multi-Atlas Riemannian Spectral Representations for Decoding Advanced Meditation States from fMRI
entry.summary: Inferring jhana-type advanced concentration absorption meditation (ACAM-J) states from fMRI data is challenging due to the spatially distributed nature of meditation-related effects, substantial inter-individual variability that can exceed within-subject state differences, and limited sample sizes. Conventional machine-learning approaches often formulate this problem as unimodal, Euclidean, atlas-based classification, thereby neglecting the non-Euclidean geometry of functional connectivity matrices and underrepresenting temporal information in functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI); these limitations can lead to suboptimal classification performance. We propose ACAM-J-MARS (\textbf{M}ulti-\textbf{A}tlas \textbf{R}iemannian \textbf{S}pectral representation), which computes functional connectivity using multiple atlases, represents symmetric positive definite (SPD) connectivity matrices on a Riemannian manifold, projects them into a log-Euclidean tangent space, and augments connectivity-derived features with low-frequency BOLD spectral energy to better resolve subtle state differences under heterogeneous variability. Evaluated on 204 segments from 22 practitioners, ACAM-J-MARS improves performance across multiple backbone models, achieving a balanced accuracy of 0.757 for early versus late ACAM-J classification and 0.545 for three-class classification, corresponding to a 10.8-point absolute improvement over the strongest baseline. These findings suggest that the proposed representation improves the decoding of advanced meditative brain states and may enable downstream applications such as closed-loop neurofeedback and real-time psychophysiological brain-computer interfaces.

entry.title: Verifiable LLM-Guided Focal SMT Solving for Quantified Arrays
entry.summary: Large language models can often identify useful semantic structure in formal artifacts, but their outputs cannot be trusted as proofs or solver decisions. We study whether LLMs can instead guide formal reasoning systems through a narrow, solver-verifiable interface. We instantiate this idea in quantified array SMT solving, where modern instantiation-based techniques can fail when key ground terms and equalities are hidden by auxiliary variables, axiom guards, and nested array terms. We observe that many instances are largely driven by a small set of focal ground terms or constraints, similar to the backdoor sets in SAT solving. Building on this, we present LinguaArray, a framework where an LLM proposes a small Semantic Focus Set (ground terms/constraints), while a conventional SMT solver remains the sole proof engine and certifies all results. LinguaArray uses these LLM-suggested, solver-validated finite sets to significantly enhance solver capability, solving additional satisfiable and unsatisfiable instances that the backend alone fails to solve. It interacts within a finite time and then falls back to the backend solver to mitigate potential regressions. Evaluation on 1015 SMT-LIB instances across five logics under 1200s timeout (including LLM latency) shows that LinguaArray solves up to 69.1% of instances and increases solved-instance counts by 105%--397% over the corresponding backends.

entry.title: Point Corrections and Wall-Crossing Geometry on the Quintic del Pezzo Threefold
entry.summary: Let $X=V_5$ be the quintic del Pezzo threefold. Along the negative zero-tilt-slope paths for rational-curve ideal classes, degree five is the first degree admitting a positive point correction. We determine the resulting degree-five outer good moduli space: it is reduced with exactly two irreducible components, a normal ten-dimensional principal branch and a smooth corrected branch $X\times\mathrm{Gr}(2,7)$. Their scheme-theoretic intersection is a normal determinantal ninefold. Along its singular locus, the principal branch has transverse rank-one $2\times 4$ determinantal singularities, while the intersection has the corresponding $2\times 3$ singularities. We construct an explicit small resolution of the principal branch as the projectivization of a rank-five extension bundle over the blow-up of the Altavilla--Petković--Rota Kuznetsov-component sixfold along its point locus. Uniform wall exclusion and point-correction bounds for degrees two through five establish the first correction threshold; the corrected degree-five factors are precisely the ideals of elliptic linear sections parametrized by $\mathrm{Gr}(2,7)$.

entry.title: Satisficing Regret Minimization in Bandits with Knapsacks
entry.summary: We study satisficing regret minimization in bandits with knapsacks (BwK), where a learner sequentially selects randomized policies, i.e., distributions over arms, to obtain mean rewards above a satisficing threshold as frequently as possible while respecting finite resource budgets. The performance is measured by satisficing regret, the cumulative deficits of the selected policies' mean rewards below this threshold. Resource constraints introduce two difficulties: an algorithm can incur linear satisficing regret even with small standard regret as deficits to the threshold cannot be compensated, and random consumption can cause early resource depletion even when policies are feasible in expectation. To address these challenges, we propose SELECTwK, a general algorithmic template that uses a BwK learning oracle algorithm with sub-linear expected (standard) regret upper bound to search for and test candidate satisficing policies (i.e., policies whose mean rewards exceed satisficing threshold and whose expected resource consumption is feasible over the time horizon). Our regret analysis, supported by an LP-duality argument, establishes that SELECTwK attains constant expected satisficing regret when a satisficing policy exists. We further introduce a stronger regret condition that bounds the expected sum of positive reward deficits to the optimal one at each time step, under which SELECTwK achieves a sharper constant bound together with a sub-linear bound in the time horizon. As a complement, SELECTwK still preserves the oracle's sub-linear expected standard regret bound if the satisficing threshold is unattainable. Finally, we establish the oracle conditions and corresponding satisficing regret bound for existing finite-armed BwK and dynamic pricing algorithms, and conduct numerical experiments on dynamic pricing with limited inventory to demonstrate the empirical performance of SELECTwK.

entry.title: Energy-Efficient FPGA Implementation of an End-to-End Cosine-Domain CNN Using High-Level Synthesis
entry.summary: The computational cost of conventional Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) limits their deployment in low-power devices for high-speed edge AI applications. This paper presents an end-to-end cosine-domain CNN (CD-CNN) architecture for energy-efficient FPGA inference using high-level synthesis (HLS). The proposed architecture performs intermediate feature extraction using real-valued DCT-domain representations, avoiding complex-valued arithmetic and intermediate inverse transforms between spectral layers. The design is implemented on a Xilinx Kintex UltraScale+ XCKU5P FPGA and evaluated against a fully spectral Fourier-domain CNN (FD-CNN) under consistent network and implementation constraints. Experiments on the MNIST and 94-class ASCII datasets show that the CD-CNN reduces normalized resource utilization and improves inference throughput on both datasets. Its energy efficiency reaches 112.91 frames/J for MNIST and 101.27 frames/J for ASCII, corresponding to improvements of $1.51\times$ and $2.76\times$, respectively, over the fully spectral FD-CNN architecture. Furthermore, compared to the previous GPU-based fully spectral CD-CNN implementation, the proposed end-to-end FPGA implementation improves energy efficiency by $12.96\times$. These results demonstrate the potential of real-valued spectral processing in the DCT domain for energy-efficient edge AI deployment.

entry.title: DiFuse: Fusing Native Diffusion Representations for Spatial Reasoning in Unified Multimodal Models
entry.summary: Unified multimodal models (UMMs) jointly support visual understanding and image generation, yet information flow between these two capabilities remains largely asymmetric: understanding representations routinely condition generation, whereas generative representations are rarely reused for multimodal reasoning. In this work, we investigate whether intermediate representations from a UMM's native diffusion branch can enhance spatial reasoning without compromising general multimodal understanding. We propose DiFuse, which selectively incorporates intermediate diffusion representations into the understanding pathway of UMMs. Through systematic layer-wise analysis, we identify which diffusion representations are most informative and where they can be integrated with minimal interference to semantic processing. Guided by these findings, DiFuse spatially aligns diffusion features with visual tokens and injects them into selected multimodal decoder layers via residual fusion. Extensive experiments on UniWorld-V1 show that, DiFuse consistently improves spatial reasoning over a matched SFT baseline while maintaining broadly comparable performance on general multimodal benchmarks. Further analyses show that these gains depend critically on the choice of diffusion representations, injection positions, and the preservation of spatial correspondence between diffusion features and visual tokens. Results on OmniGen2 further demonstrate the transferability of DiFuse across unified multimodal architectures. Overall, our findings show that native diffusion representations can provide complementary spatial cues for multimodal reasoning when selectively integrated in a structure-preserving manner.

entry.title: Neuromorphic Realization of Best Response in Finite-Action Games
entry.summary: We develop a mechanistic dynamical-systems formulation of best response in finite-action games with relational structure on the action set. The proposed neuromorphic decision dynamics realize best response as the stable outcome of an internal state-space process, rather than as an externally imposed choice rule. This provides a deterministic account of commitment formation, symmetry resolution through basins of attraction, and hysteresis and decision persistence under perturbations. For action spaces with circulant coupling, we prove using Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction that the action-coupling operator determines which components of evidence govern decision formation. We further show that the dynamics implicitly compute a geometry-aware utility, converge exponentially to the corresponding best response, and switch only when evidence is sufficiently strong. In contrast, supplying the same geometry-aware utility directly to logit dynamics does not recover these properties, showing that relational structure must be embedded in the decision mechanism itself. We illustrate the framework in a repeated coverage game, prove that the induced game is an exact potential game, and show that its Nash equilibria are reached by the neuromorphic decision dynamics.

entry.title: Quantum-Relativistic Anomalous Proper Time
entry.summary: We investigate surprising consequences of the hypothesis that gravity and proper time obey the quantum superposition principle. We show that, for a massive body prepared in a superposition of two positions and post-selected in a suitable final state, the elapsed proper time in another region of space can assume an anomalous effective value lying outside the range allowed by classical general relativity. Remarkably, the effective elapsed proper time can even become negative, corresponding to an effective evolution backward in time. We also propose an experiment to observe an anomalous effective proper time associated with the internal degrees of freedom of a quantum particle in an interferometer under Earth's gravitational field. The proposed experiment is, in principle, feasible with current technology, and its realization could provide the first experimental evidence of an interplay between quantum mechanics and general relativity beyond the effects of the Newtonian potential in flat spacetime.

entry.title: Twirled and swirled worlds: a compositional approach
entry.summary: Twirled and swirled worlds describe generalised probabilistic theories (GPTs) restricted by symmetry-imposed superselection rules. We extend these constructions to a fully compositional setting for finite-dimensional GPTs and compact groups, treating states, effects, and multipartite transformations uniformly as processes. We distinguish system actions from process-space actions. We define actions on a theory as a whole by requiring the corresponding process-space actions to respect sequential and parallel composition. Averaging physical theory actions defines twirling, while averaging nonphysical theory actions defines swirling. We show that invariant subtheories might not satisfy process tomography, and establish conditions under which they do, involving invariant dynamically faithful states or internal classical reference frames. For locally tomographic parent theories, we prove that every theory symmetry admits a representation by linear system actions and that the invariant subtheory satisfies process tomography. An invariant multipartite process space fails local tomography if and only if some bipartition has sides sharing a non-trivial irreducible representation. We characterise when ancillary systems are necessary, which representations they must carry, and when entanglement is required for ancilla-free process tomography. We develop a framework for unifying twirled subtheories and extend incoherent simulations to compact groups. Finally, we recover bilocal classical theory as a twirled subtheory of classical theory and real quantum theory as a swirled subtheory of complex quantum theory, deriving their tomographic properties from their representation structure.

entry.title: Symmetry-breaking in a discrete-choice LQG mean field game
entry.summary: Mean-field games provide a continuum framework for modeling the dynamics of large, interacting populations of non-cooperative agents. This paper studies symmetry-breaking in a finite-horizon, two-choice min-LQG mean-field game in which identical agents with linear stochastic dynamics choose one of two equally desirable terminal destinations, while trading off control effort against social pressure to conform. The model has an odd symmetry between the two destinations and therefore always admits a symmetric, dynamic Nash equilibrium in which the population splits evenly between them, producing a deadlock collective state at final time. Numerical studies have suggested that, as the penalty for social nonconformity increases, this symmetric equilibrium loses stability as a fixed point of an associated scalar, self-consistency map, and asymmetric consensus Nash equilibria emerge, where most agents select the same destination. By analyzing the linearized forward-backward PDE system through the scalar map representation, we provide a proof of this loss of stability of the symmetric equilibrium. Together with the odd symmetry of the map, this implies the existence of symmetry-broken mean-field game equilibria corresponding to consensus on either destination.

entry.title: Ground-state spaces of generalized stabilizer codes
entry.summary: In this paper, we determine the complete ground-state spaces for a broad class of generalized stabilizer quantum models defined over CW-decompositions of non-compact manifolds of arbitrary dimensions and topological type. We introduce a $C^*$-algebraic framework in which the quantum spin algebra $\A$ is realized as the twisted group $C^*$-algebra of an infinite discrete Pauli module $P$ endowed with a symplectic structure. We establish a correspondence between stabilizer models and isotropic subgroups of $P$: Every Lagrangian extension of such a subgroup determines a $C^*$-diagonal of $\A$, whose Weyl groupoid encodes the dynamics through a continuous 1-cocycle. This realization yields an explicit family of extremal ground-states for every admissible Lagrangian model, together with their decomposition into sectors. When the sector space is $T_0$, this gives a complete characterization of the ground-state spaces. We also prove that every Lagrangian stabilizer model admits a unique frustration-free ground state with a spectral gap. Our framework applies in arbitrary dimension, including higher abelian quantum doubles, homological codes, and a broad class of stabilizer models.

entry.title: The As-If Machine: Personalized counterfactuals make distant policy risks feel close
entry.summary: Life experiences can shape policy attitudes, but we only live one life. Citizens may therefore fail to support policies addressing risks they have never personally experienced. Narratives can make such risks immediate and personal, but personalized stories remain difficult to produce at scale. Here we ask whether AI can make distant scenarios feel concrete by simulating a participant's life as if that scenario occurred. We present the As-If Machine (AIM), a multi-agent system through which people co-write personalized counterfactual narratives---stories about their own lives under different policy futures. In two pre-registered and quota-matched experiments on science funding (N=1,007) and satellite cybersecurity (N=894), we compared AIM with two controls: reading an expert-written vignette on the same topic and co-writing with AIM about an unrelated topic. AIM increased psychological closeness---how close a risk feels to the self---by nearly identical margins in the two domains (0.36 and 0.38 standard deviations (SDs) against the vignette, 0.80 and 0.90 against unrelated writing). AIM increased psychological closeness even among participants with unfavorable views of AI. For policy attitudes, AIM's effects were 0.16 SDs against the vignette and 0.10 SDs (n.s.) against unrelated writing for science funding; the corresponding effects for satellite cybersecurity were 0.54 and 0.67 SDs. Across 23,496 human-AI autocomplete interactions, participants and the system played distinct roles: AIM supplied concrete detail that grounded the scenario, and participants supplied first-person perspective and emotion. Co-writing with the As-If Machine makes distant policy risks feel close.

entry.title: Gibbs measures on Cayley trees and homoclinic orbits
entry.summary: We study the question of existence and multiplicity of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures on Cayley trees with spin space $\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that, under a natural summability assumption on the interaction function, there are always at least two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying two natural symmetry conditions. Moreover, any two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying a suitable non-degeneracy assumption can be superimposed and produce infinitely many other homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures. When the interaction function $Q$ has bounded support in $\mathbb{Z}$, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a symplectomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, where $n$ is the smallest natural number such that $Q(i)=0$ for every $i>n$. For $n=1$, results from symbolic dynamics and horseshoes imply the existence of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures whose single-site marginal is concentrated near an arbitrary finite subset of $N\mathbb{Z}$, where $N$ is a sufficiently large integer. In the case of interaction functions with infinite support, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a Lagrangian correspondence on the cotangent bundle of a Banach space.

entry.title: The Affective Bridge: Preserving Speech Representations while Enhancing Deepfake Detection via emotional Constraints
entry.summary: Speech deepfake detection (DFD) has benefited from diverse acoustic and semantic speech representations, many of which encode valuable speech information and are costly to train. Prior work has shown that affective cues improve DFD, yet existing approaches either fuse emotion with other task-specific features in complex pipelines or directly fine-tune representations toward DFD objectives, risking distortion of the original speech representations that support downstream tasks such as speaker verification (SV) or automatic speech recognition (ASR). We propose a simpler approach: fine-tuning speech encoders on emotion recognition alone-without any DFD supervision, and training a lightweight support vector machine (SVM) on the frozen emotion-tuned representations for DFD. This preserves the original representation capacity for downstream tasks such as SV and ASR, while emergently improving DFD performance. Crucially, we find that emotion is uniquely effective as this bridging task: replacing it with speaker identity even degrades DFD performance, demonstrating that the benefit stems from emotion's role as a natural bridge between speech representation and DFD. Experiments on FakeOrReal and In-the-Wild show accuracy improvements of up to 6\% and 2\% with corresponding EER reductions, while analysis on ASVspoof 2019 LA reveals dataset-specific speaker bias in the real-speech subset. Code is available at \href{https://github.com/myxp-lyp/The-Affective-Bridge-Unifying-Feature-Representations-for-Speech-Deepfake-Detection}{GitHub repository}.

entry.title: Semantic Path Orders are Generalized Weighted Path Orders
entry.summary: Monotonic semantic path orders (MSPOs) are powerful reduction orders, but their effective use in theorem proving and termination analysis raises three issues: efficient comparison of terms, ground totality, and a reduction-pair formulation. Inspired by weighted path orders (WPOs), we introduce generalized weighted path orders (GWPOs) which encompass both WPOs and MSPOs. GWPOs and MSPOs coincide as classes of reduction orders, thereby yielding efficient and ground-total subclasses of MSPOs. We further formulate the reduction-pair version of the GWPO for the dependency pair method, from which a reduction-pair version of the MSPO is obtained. In contrast to the reduction-order setting, the correspondence between GWPOs and MSPOs no longer fully carries over, establishing the GWPO as a framework of independent interest. Effectiveness of the resulting reduction pairs is assessed by standard termination benchmarks.

entry.title: Local Convergence of Triadic Closures of Sparse Random Graphs
entry.summary: Triadic closure is a natural mechanism for modeling the clustering phenomenon observed in many real-world networks. Given a possibly random undirected graph $H$, we consider pairs of non-adjacent vertices that have a common neighbor. Conditional on $H$, each such pair is joined by an edge independently and simultaneously, with a probability depending on the degrees of its endpoints and on the number of their common neighbors. The resulting graph is called a triadic closure of $H$. We study the effect of this operation on local convergence. More precisely, we prove that if a sequence of potentially random finite undirected graphs of $\left( H_n \right)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ converges locally in probability to a rooted graph $H^*$, then the corresponding sequence of triadic closures converges locally in probability to the same triadic closure of $H^*$. As a consequence, we obtain a general limit theorem for the clustering coefficients of triadic closures. In particular, we show that the triadic closures can have a strictly positive limiting clustering coefficients even when the limiting clustering coefficients of the parent graph sequence is zero. Finally, we apply our results to several classical sparse random graph models including Erdős-Rényi, configuration, preferential attachment models and compute the limiting clustering coefficients of their triadic closures.

entry.title: Rank three representations of Painlevé systems: I. Wild character varieties
entry.summary: We give explicit cubic equations for the wild character varieties corresponding to the rank 3 representations of Painlevé equations, and compare them to the ones of their classical rank 2 representations.

entry.title: Diffusion Processes on $p$-Wasserstein Space over Banach Space
entry.summary: To study diffusion processes on the p-Wasserstein space $\mathscr P_p$ for $p\in [1,\infty)$ over a separable, reflexive Banach space $X$, we present a criterion on the quasi-regularity of Dirichlet forms in $L^2(\mathscr P_p,Λ)$ for a reference probability $Λ$ on $\mathscr P_p$. It is formulated in terms of an upper bound condition with the uniform norm of the intrinsic derivative. We find a versatile class of quasi-regular local Dirichlet forms on $\mathscr P_p$ by using images of Dirichlet forms on the tangent space $L^p(X\to X,μ_0)$ at a reference point $μ_0\in\mathscr P_p$. The Ornstein--Uhlenbeck type Dirichlet form and process on $\mathscr P_2$ are an important example in this class. We derive an $L^2$-estimate for the corresponding heat kernel and an integration by parts formula for the invariant measure.

entry.title: Nucleon Wave Functions from QCD Vacuum Topology
entry.summary: Instantons, as topologically nontrivial gauge field configurations, provide a microscopic mechanism for chiral symmetry breaking and the $U_A(1)$ anomaly in QCD. Within the instanton liquid model (ILM), instantons generate multi-fermion interactions governed by their density and size. Using this framework, we develop a microscopic description of the nucleon based on instanton-induced quark--quark correlations. We derive the diquark interaction kernels arising from single instantons and instanton--anti-instanton molecules, revealing a strong attraction in the scalar channel and weaker correlations in the spin-one channels. Embedding these interactions in a covariant, permutation-symmetric Bethe--Salpeter--Faddeev equation yields a nucleon mass $m_N=939.53~{\rm MeV}$, with a predominantly scalar-diquark component ($98\%$) and a small axial-vector admixture ($2\%$) around the mass pole. Despite its small weight, the small admixture generates substantial spin--isospin interference, yielding an axial charge $g_A=1.265$, close to experiment. The resulting covariant amplitude is analytically continued to the light front to obtain the leading three-quark wave function. The corresponding unpolarized, helicity, and transversity parton distributions, along with their QCD-evolved moments, provide a direct connection to lattice QCD calculations and global-fit analyses. Our results show that the topology of the QCD vacuum organizes not only the nucleon mass and spin structure, but also its leading valence partonic content, providing a microscopic foundation for a more complete description including confinement and higher Fock components.

entry.title: Infrared behavior of the photon yield in nonlinear Compton scattering
entry.summary: Nonlinear Compton scattering is the process of emission of a single photon by a charge driven by an intense laser field. Here, we study the infrared behavior of the photon yield emitted via nonlinear Compton scattering. We first consider the idealized case of an electron in the presence of a plane wave and derive an analytical expression of the total yield in the form of a double integral over the laser phase. As it is known, the total yield is finite in the experimentally common case of a plane-wave laser field without a dc component whereas it diverges logarithmically in the complementary case of so-called unipolar fields. The divergence is found here to correspond to the longer-and-longer formation lengths of emitted photons with lower-and-lower frequency. Interestingly, we also find that the corrections to the Volkov states stemming from the fact that the field is unipolar cancel out in the computation of the probability of nonlinear Compton scattering, which is in agreement with the fact that in the classical limit the expression of the photon yield is independent of whether the plane wave is unipolar or not. Then, we pass to the more realistic case of an electron in a tightly-focused laser beam by assuming that the electron is ultrarelativistic. In this case we determine analytically the classical angular distribution of the yield of photons with an energy larger than a fixed value $\hbarω_m$ as a double integral over the electron's trajectory. After obtaining also the corresponding quantum expression of the angular distribution of the photon yield within the quasiclassical approximation, we determine analytically the leading-order quantum correction, which scales as $\hbarω_m/\varepsilon$, where $\varepsilon$ is the initial electron energy. Considerations on the experimental feasibility of the found results in the latter situations are also presented.

entry.title: The Locality Trade-off in Masked Patch Self-Distillation
entry.summary: Masked patch self-distillation is a key component of modern vision foundation models, including DINOv2 and DINOv3, yet its implications for local visual information remain unclear. We show that its semantic benefits can coexist with a scale-dependent locality cost. Using two annotation-free diagnostics, we distinguish recoverable local appearance from spatial correspondence. In smaller models, adding iBOT substantially weakens patch correspondence while largely preserving appearance decodability. In larger models, correspondence improves, but pixel and texture evidence becomes less linearly accessible in deep features. Thus, scaling changes the form of the locality cost rather than uniformly eliminating it. Our analysis of Gram anchoring further shows that preserving patch relations does not guarantee simultaneous improvements in both properties. These findings motivate evaluating and designing visual representations around the complementary demands of semantic abstraction, appearance preservation, and spatial correspondence. Our code is available at https://github.com/winci-ai/jea.

entry.title: Regional Anchor Routing for Multi-Object Motion Transfer
entry.summary: Compositional motion transfer requires a model to extract motions from multiple reference videos, and apply each motion to a user-specified object in one target scene. Existing methods normally struggle to reliably assign different reference motions to the correct target objects, thus a motion intended for one object may affect another. Meanwhile, some motion-specific tuning approaches are still facing another issue: they must run a new optimization whenever the reference video changes, making repeated transfers inefficient. To address these limitations, we propose RART, a framework that unifies object-wise motion extraction, target-region anchoring, and frame-aligned injection into a frozen video Diffusion Transformer for multi-object motion transfer. For each reference motion, RART extracts temporally ordered features from the masked reference video, and then conditions them on the target first-frame mask to form mask-anchored motion tokens. Frame-aligned motion cross-attention allows each generated frame to read only the motion tokens at the corresponding time slots, composing all object motions in one denoising process. During training, a motion-attention routing loss encourages each target region to attend to its corresponding motion tokens and reduces interference between objects. Therefore, RART can handle novel reference-target combinations without per-video optimization. Experiments show that RART achieves accurate motion preservation, efficient inference, and strong compositional generalization.

entry.title: Complete regular dessins and non-metacyclic bicyclic 2-groups with cyclic commutator subgroup
entry.summary: We study complete regular dessins with underlying graph ${\mathcal K}_{2^e,2^f}$, where $e\geq f\geq 2$, whose automorphism groups are non-metacyclic. Together with the cases of coprime orders and odd-prime-power orders, this is one of the basic classes needed for Jones's open classification problem for regular dessins of complete bipartite graphs. Within the 2-power case, the present paper treats the subcase in which the commutator subgroup is cyclic; it is the first of three papers devoted to the non-metacyclic case. Our approach is group-theoretic. The automorphism group $G$ of a regular dessin of ${\mathcal K}_{2^e,2^f}$ admits an exact bicyclic factorization $G=\langle b\rangle\langle w\rangle$ of type $(2^e,2^f)$ with $\langle b\rangle\cap\langle w\rangle=1$. For a fixed group $G$, two exact generating pairs give isomorphic dessins exactly when they lie in the same orbit under ${\rm A}ut(G)$. Thus the classification reduces to three group-theoretic tasks: determining the isomorphism classes of the possible groups $G$, characterizing their exact bicyclic generating pairs, and computing $|{\rm A}ut(G)|$. Berkovich and Janko divided the relevant non-metacyclic groups, through parameterized presentations, according to whether the commutator subgroup is cyclic, contains a cyclic subgroup of index $2$, or contains a cyclic subgroup of index $2^r$ with $r>1$. However, their classification does not identify which parameter values in these presentations define isomorphic groups; this problem was raised by Janko in {J}. We carry out these steps for the cyclic-commutator case. This settles Janko's isomorphism-classification problem in this case and yields a complete classification and enumeration of the corresponding regular dessins.

entry.title: Composable Device-Independent Quantum Digital Signatures
entry.summary: Extending device-independent (DI) quantum cryptography to composably support all fundamental information security objectives is crucial for secure quantum networks. Achieving this goal requires composable quantum digital signatures (QDSs), which support integrity, authenticity, and nonrepudiation when integrated into quantum networks. Yet existing QDS protocols generally rely on assumptions about the underlying quantum devices, while their security analyses remain largely restricted to stand-alone settings, leaving related-key attacks on the underlying linear feedback shift register (LFSR)-based Toeplitz authentication unaddressed. Here, we establish the first composable security framework for QDS within constructive cryptography, and realize the corresponding ideal QDS resource by developing a DI-QDS protocol employing one-time universal hashing and multi-channel multiplexing. We further derive a related-key security bound for the underlying LFSR-based Toeplitz authentication, thereby establishing unforgeability while extending the forgery boundary considered in previous QDS security analyses. We also demonstrate the practical feasibility of our DI-QDS protocol under realistic quantum network conditions in the finite-size regime, with numerical simulations showing that it enables efficient signing of multibit documents over metropolitan-scale distances. Our results establish QDS as a composable cryptographic primitive and extend DI quantum cryptography to support the full range of information security objectives with composable security guarantees in future quantum networks.

entry.title: Gen-Searcher: Reinforcing Agentic Search for Image Generation
entry.summary: Recent image generation models have shown strong capabilities in generating high-fidelity and photorealistic images. However, they are fundamentally constrained by frozen internal knowledge, thus often failing on real-world scenarios that are knowledge-intensive or require up-to-date information. In this paper, we present Gen-Searcher, as the first attempt to train a search-augmented image generation agent, which performs multi-hop reasoning and search to collect the textual knowledge and reference images needed for grounded generation. To achieve this, we construct a tailored data pipeline and curate two high-quality datasets, Gen-Searcher-SFT-10k and Gen-Searcher-RL-6k, containing diverse search-intensive prompts and corresponding ground-truth synthesis images. We further introduce KnowGen, a comprehensive benchmark that explicitly requires search-grounded external knowledge for image generation and evaluates models from multiple dimensions. Based on these resources, we train Gen-Searcher with SFT followed by agentic reinforcement learning with dual reward feedback, which combines text-based and image-based rewards to provide more stable and informative learning signals for GRPO training. Experiments show that Gen-Searcher brings substantial gains, improving Qwen-Image by around 16 points on KnowGen and 15 points on WISE. We hope this work can serve as an open foundation for search agents in image generation, and we fully open-source our data, models, and code.

entry.title: Derivative-Informed Dimension Reduction of Stochastic Differential Equations: A Path-Space Sensitivity Approach
entry.summary: Uncertainty in the drift of a stochastic differential equation (SDE) induces uncertainty in statistical observables defined as expected functionals on path space. We propose a derivative-informed method for identifying low-dimensional structure in the drift-to-observable map, with the aim of improving the tractability of uncertainty quantification. This approach can be viewed as a generalization of the active subspace method to infinite-dimensional input spaces and to path-space observables of SDEs. Representing uncertainty in the drift by random perturbations in a Hilbert space, we construct a path-space sensitivity operator using first-order Fréchet derivatives of the observable with respect to the perturbation. We establish conditions under which the leading eigenfunctions of this operator correspond to directions of maximum mean squared sensitivity of the observable, thus enabling low-dimensional approximation with certified error bounds. We further introduce a martingale control variate of the Fréchet derivative that reduces error in sample-based estimators of the operator. Using a Galerkin scheme for numerical discretization, we show that reduced representations of the drift from the derivative-informed basis yield more accurate approximations of mean first hitting times of SDEs than the Karhunen-Loève expansion of the same truncation order.

entry.title: HWF Analysis of TRN Black Holes
entry.summary: We extend the horizon wave-function (HWF) formalism to a spherically symmetric, charged, spinless quantum source in $\mathcal{D} + 1$ dimensional spacetime geometry and construct the HWFs associated with inner- as well as outer-horizons of the Tangherlini--Reissner--Nordström (TRN) black hole. The corresponding black hole formation probabilities, $P_{\rm BH}^{\pm}$, are also calculated and their sensitivities due to various source parameters including charge, mass, and $\mathcal{D}$ are analysed as well. Our analysis reveals that the ratio of inner- to outer-horizon probabilities, $P_{\rm BH}^{-}/P_{\rm BH}^{+}$, changes drastically from being unity as the source departs away from being in the extremal limit defined by $α$ ($\to 1$ for extremal case). Furthermore, black hole formation probabilities are found to be highly suppressed for higher values of $\mathcal{D}$, particularly for the source mass, $m \lesssim Λ_{\mathcal{D}}$, e.g., for $α= 0.5$, the ratio, $P_{\rm BH}^{+}(\mathcal{D} = 5)/P_{\rm BH}^{+}(\mathcal{D}=10)$ turn out to be approximately $2.95\times10^3$, $117$, and $3.35$ respectively for $m/Λ_{\mathcal{D}} = 0.5, 1$ and $2$, with $Λ_{\mathcal{D}}$ being the reduced gravity scale associated with $\mathcal{D}$ spatial-dimensions.

entry.title: Conic-Lifting for Learning-rate-free Convex Optimization
entry.summary: A central topic in online and stochastic optimization is to design algorithms that do not require tuning of hyperparameters. Successful strategies in online learning include AdaGrad-style learning rates, Conic Blackwell algorithms, and parameter-free algorithms. However, these classes require different, often difficult, analyses. We develop a unifying family of Online Convex Optimization (OCO) algorithms that require no user-tuned learning rate on convex domains that may be unbounded. The construction lifts the domain to a cone by adding one scalar coordinate, an idea going back to Blackwell (1954). The lifted subgradients are orthogonal to the corresponding lifted decisions, leaving the comparator scale free to optimize in the regret analysis. Applying Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (FTRL) and Online Mirror Descent (OMD) on the cone recovers Conic Blackwell Algorithm (CBA) and Conic Blackwell Algorithm Plus (CBA$^+$) on bounded domains in Hilbert spaces and extends them to finite-dimensional normed spaces with a strongly convex squared norm. For arbitrary nonempty closed convex domains in these spaces, a known gradient bound yields parameter-free regret guarantees. Surprisingly, on an unconstrained Hilbert space, the construction recovers the Krichevsky--Trofimov (KT) coin-betting algorithm exactly. We also give a parameter-free algorithm for unconstrained domains that requires no gradient bound.

entry.title: SemMSA: Latent Semantic-Aided Robust Multimodal Sentiment Analysis with Incomplete Data
entry.summary: Recent research on Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (MSA) has focused on learning from language, visual, and acoustic modalities with incomplete data to infer human sentiment. Most studies typically compensate for missing information by reconstructing modality features or designing complicated fusion mechanisms. However, these methods still suffer from spurious generation and noisy guidance due to the lack of high-level semantic grounding in partially observed multimodal evidence. To address these issues, we propose SemMSA, a latent semantic-aided framework that constructs rich sentiment-relevant semantics with LLMs, fully integrating with all modalities via anchor-free spectral alignment. It mainly consists of Cross-modal Semantic Refinement (CSR) and Cross-modal Spectral Alignment (CSA). Specifically, CSR first adaptively extracts visual and acoustic representations by corresponding adapters to form a unified multimodal prefix with language in the frozen LLM embedding space. It then iteratively produces continuous discriminative semantic states through a token-efficient latent refinement process without decoding explicit text. Next, CSA simultaneously aligns the refined semantics with all modalities by enhancing the dominant spectral component of their kernel Gram matrix. This captures global nonlinear dependencies among all representations without relying on a predefined anchor modality. In addition, an instance-level spectral separation constraint preserves cross-sample discriminability and mitigates representation collapse. Extensive experiments on SIMS, MOSI, and MOSEI benchmarks demonstrate that SemMSA achieves state-of-the-art performance.

entry.title: CCFormer: Efficient Cross-Field Interaction and Hierarchical Sequence Compression for Industrial Recommendation at Tencent
entry.summary: Industrial candidate-ranking systems must combine long user behavior histories with heterogeneous user and item features under strict computational budgets. We propose CCFormer, a structured interaction architecture that separates cross-field retrieval from intra-history modeling. Feature-field-separated cross-attention allows user and target queries to read an evolving history hierarchy, while local subspace token mixing contextualizes history tokens independently of candidate targets. Hierarchical sequence compression reduces the number of history tokens and provides multi-scale historical context for subsequent interactions. Experiments on two public benchmarks show higher mean AUC than the evaluated baselines, while experiments on a large-scale industrial dataset show a favorable accuracy-compute trade-off and higher training throughput than HSTU. Online A/B tests across four recommendation and advertising scenarios report system-level improvements of up to 3.57% in click-through rate, 3.86% in page views, and 1.71% in advertising revenue relative to the corresponding production baselines. CCFormer has been fully deployed in all four scenarios, demonstrating its practical scalability and effectiveness in large-scale recommendation systems.

entry.title: Label-free Monitoring of Nucleoid Dynamics of Bacteria for Drug Screening Using Holography
entry.summary: We introduce holographic microscopy (HM) as a compact, low-cost, label-free, non-specific alternative to fluorescence microscopy (FM) for quantifying bacterial physiological responses during drug screening. Using the regularized inverse holographic volumetric reconstruction (RIHVR) framework, we extract phase maps from HM images and then invert the reconstructed phase to generate fluorescence-like contrast, in which bright inverted-phase regions correspond to bacterial nucleoid content captured by FM signals. We show that this relationship holds across multiple bacterial species, growth stages, drug treatments, and post-treatment time points, demonstrating that HM can consistently capture nucleoid associated structural information without fluorescent labeling. Because HM phase images contain both whole-cell refractive-index information and internal nucleoid-associated contrast, they enable simultaneous quantification of cell boundaries, cell length, nucleoid size, and nucleoid occupancy. These measurements allow drug-induced changes in bacterial morphology and nucleoid organization to be monitored over time. Unlike FM, which can suffer from photobleaching and may perturb live cells through phototoxicity, HM relies on refractive-index variations and maintains stable signal quality for long-term live-cell imaging. By linking label-free phase imaging to nucleoid-scale physiological readouts, this work establishes a path toward automated, high-throughput, and experimentally simpler bacterial drug-screening assays.

entry.title: Norm of resonance states in quantum scattering and electromagnetic systems
entry.summary: Resonance states spatially diverge and are thus not square integrable. Instead, their norm is defined by the biorthogonal scalar product of left and right states. We replace the corresponding volume integral over infinite space by a convenient boundary integral in piecewise-homogeneous systems and apply this procedure to diverse physical settings. For a quantum particle in any number of dimensions we treat hard-wall and piecewise-constant potentials. For electromagnetic systems with piecewise-homogeneous material properties, we consider three-dimensional and effectively two-dimensional cavities.

entry.title: From the Transformer to a Formal Semantics of Coordinated Transformations
entry.summary: We develop a formal semantics for a general class of coordinated systems of parameterized transformations, taking the Transformer as a paradigmatic starting point but abstracting from its particular mathematical instantiation. Representational vectors receive both extensional reference and ordered intensional interpretations, while parameter structures acquire relative, second-level interpretations that determine how argument properties are preserved, replaced, or combined. This yields the notion of a transforming concept: a parameterized transformation whose numerical action is coordinated with a corresponding property-level map. We then distinguish the common algebraic-semantic core of these systems from their architecture-specific functional organization, allowing different mathematical instantiations and mechanical realizations of the same abstract system type. The framework is applied to attention heads and residual connections, providing semantic explanations that depend only on the shared algebraic-semantic core and their local functional organization and therefore generalize beyond the standard Transformer. These analyses also reveal the modularity of the framework: complex architectures can be decomposed into simpler semantically coordinated subsystems whose organization may recur across different abstract system types.

entry.title: Next-to-leading-order QCD study of $e^+e^- \to η_c + c\bar{c}$ at $B$ factories
entry.summary: We study the process $e^+e^- \to γ^\ast \to η_c + c\bar{c} + X$ at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD within the framework of nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD) factorization, retaining the color-singlet contribution at leading order in the heavy-quark relative velocity $v$. At the $e^+e^-$ collision energy $\sqrt{s} = 10.6~\mathrm{GeV}$, with $m_c = 1.5~\mathrm{GeV}$ and $μ_R = 2m_c$, the direct cross section increases from $58.7~\mathrm{fb}$ at leading order (LO) to $118~\mathrm{fb}$ at NLO, corresponding to a $K$ factor of approximately $2.0$. Including the radiative feed-down contributions of the $J/ψ$ and $h_c(1P)$ states yields an estimated prompt production rate of $131~\mathrm{fb}$. The NLO corrections substantially enhance both the angular and momentum distributions, while the momentum spectrum retains a similar overall profile. These results establish an NLO color-singlet baseline for $η_c$ production associated with open charm at Belle II, complementary to studies of charmonium production in hadronic collisions.

entry.title: Detection of HNCOH+ in the interstellar medium
entry.summary: Only five out of the $\sim$350 molecules detected in the interstellar medium (ISM) carry the isocyanate functional group (NCO), the essential substructure of peptide bonds in proteins. Among them are isocyanic acid (HNCO) and its most stable N-protonated isomer H$_2$NCO$^+$. Previous studies have predicted that the O-protonated isomer HNCOH$^+$ should be present in the ISM; yet this species has remained elusive. We search for the metastable HNCOH$^+$ towards the Galactic Center molecular cloud G+0.693-0.027, where H$_2$NCO$^+$ has already been detected. We use an ultra-deep broadband spectral survey carried out towards G+0.693-0.027 with the Yebes 40-m, IRAM 30-m and APEX telescopes covering nearly 150 GHz of bandwidth between 31 and 275 GHz. We report the first detection of HNCOH$^+$ in the ISM with a column density of $N$ = (9.9 $\pm$ 0.5)$\times$10$^{12}$ cm$^{-2}$, which corresponds to a molecular abundance relative to H$_2$ of (7.3$^{+1.3} _{-1.0}$)$\times$10$^{-11}$. With the measured H$_2$NCO$^+$ column density of $N$ = (2.6 $\pm$ 0.3) $\times 10^{12}$ cm$^{-2}$, this yields a HNCOH$^+$/H$_2$NCO$^+$ ratio of 3.8$^{+0.5} _{-0.4}$. This result is consistent with recent kinetic calculations that favour the formation of HNCOH$^+$ over H$_2$NCO$^+$. The detection of HNCOH$^+$ in the ISM broadens the inventory of molecules known to contain the isocyanate functional group and reinforces recent works showing that isomer abundances in the ISM do not necessarily correlate with thermodynamic stability.
